speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our assessment, could you describe exactly how your walking and coordination have been affected, and when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms on the right side suggest a focal lesion. How long have you been experiencing these issues, and do you notice any weakness, numbness, or vision changes along with the clumsiness?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history is significant; natalizumab carries a risk for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Given your specific medication and symptoms, have you noticed any new visual disturbances or changes in your cognitive function recently? Also, when was your last MRI of your brain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of fever or infection makes PML less likely, but your weakness is asymmetric. Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your right arm, or any changes in your vision, hearing, or balance specifically? Also, did you mention you were taking natalizumab for Crohn's disease? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain.
